title: Trump Administration Bars Correspondents from CNN, Politico, and MS NOW from White House
snippet: In a dramatic escalation against press access, White House security revoked credentials for reporters from three major news organizations a day after President Donald Trump labeled their reporting 'fake news.'
content:
WASHINGTON — Access to the White House was abruptly revoked for correspondents representing CNN, MS NOW, and Politico on Saturday, signaling a sharp escalation in President Donald Trump’s ongoing battles with the press corp.

Journalists arriving for work on Saturday morning were turned away at security checkpoints, where officers informed them that their press credentials had been deactivated and subsequently confiscated. The move follows a Friday decree from President Trump, who posted on social media that he was banning the three outlets due to reporting he claimed was 'fake news.'

Among those denied entry were CNN senior White House reporter Betsy Klein, MS NOW correspondent Akayla Gardner, and Politico reporter Cheyenne Haslett. Gardner reported that her hard pass was disabled after she cleared initial security gates, noting that Secret Service officers told her the directive was 'above them.' Klein similarly reported having her badge confiscated before being instructed to contact the press office for further information.

First Amendment Defense and Media Backlash

The sudden action drew immediate outrage from press freedom advocates and triggered promises of legal retaliation from the affected outlets. Politico Editor-in-Chief Jonathan Greenberger affirmed in a memo to staff that the newsroom would 'vigorously defend our First Amendment rights,' while statements from CNN and MS NOW reinforced their intent to pursue all legal avenues to uphold independent journalism.

Jacqui Heinrich, president of the White House Correspondents' Association, urged the administration to reverse course immediately, warning that the policy sets a dangerous precedent for government accountability.

'The implications extend beyond these organizations: a standard used to exclude one news outlet because of its coverage could be applied to any outlet in the future,' Heinrich said in a statement. 'The American people, through a free and independent press, must be able to scrutinize those elected to power.'

An Escalating Strategy Against News Organizations

Media law experts emphasized that the administration's aggressive tactics mark a significant departure from long-standing presidential traditions regarding press access. Amy Kristin Sanders, a media law professor at Penn State University, stated that the administration's efforts to penalize news outlets far surpass those of any modern American presidency, creating a chilling effect on reporting nationwide.

Saturday's ban is the latest in a series of punitive actions directed at news organizations during Trump's second term. The administration previously restricted access for The Associated Press following a dispute over regional naming conventions, prompting an ongoing lawsuit. The administration has also pursued separate litigation and regulatory pressure against entities including The New York Times, The Wall Street Journal, and ABC.
